stem: A 72-year-old patient receives an unchanged regimen of a drug eliminated through the kidneys. Renal excretory function falls, and subsequent measurements show a rising drug concentration with toxicity. There has been no dosing or administration error. Which of the following most directly explains the new concentration pattern?

options.text: Reduced elimination requires a falling concentration of the drug
options.explanation: This reverses the consequence of impaired removal. With continued administration, reduced elimination supports a higher concentration rather than forcing the concentration to fall.
options.label: A
options.misconception: Reverses the concentration consequence of reduced removal during continued drug administration.

options.text: Stable elimination explains the effect of declining renal function
options.explanation: Stable elimination would not connect the known reduction in excretory function to the rising concentration. The drug’s dependence on the kidneys makes reduced removal relevant.
options.label: B
options.misconception: Assumes unchanged elimination explains accumulation following a decline in renal excretory function.

options.text: Increased elimination directly explains the observed drug toxicity
options.explanation: The concentration rises despite unchanged administration, favoring reduced removal. Increased elimination would not explain the observed accumulation that accompanies the decline in renal function.
options.label: C
options.misconception: Attributes the rising drug concentration and toxicity to increased rather than reduced elimination.

options.text: Reduced elimination permits retention of the administered drug
options.explanation: Reduced renal function can decrease elimination of a drug that depends on renal excretion. Continued administration then permits accumulation, explaining the rising concentration and toxicity.
options.label: D
options.misconception: No misconception: reduced renal elimination permits retention during an unchanged regimen of a renally cleared drug.

options.text: Increased elimination permits retention of the administered drug
options.explanation: Increasing elimination would oppose retention rather than cause it. The observed loss of renal excretory function explains accumulation through a reduction in drug removal.
options.label: E
options.misconception: Treats increased drug elimination as a cause of retention instead of a process opposing it.

context: Learning objective: Connect declining renal excretion to drug accumulation and toxicity under an unchanged regimen. Reduced renal function can decrease elimination of a drug that depends on renal excretion. Continued administration then permits accumulation, explaining the rising concentration and toxicity.
